chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan al-Nishapuri, from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Safwan ibn Yahya and Uthman ibn Isa, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said:

I was in the company of Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), so he said to me: Indeed, Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: A man is fortunate if he lives to see his successor from his own self. Then he pointed with his hand to his son Ali and said: This is he, and Allah has shown me my successor from my own self.

key_terms.أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim, a title for Imam Musa al-Kadhim
key_terms.خَلْفَهُ: His successor or successor from his progeny

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim say about seeing one's successor from one's own progeny?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the continuity of the Imamate within the progeny of Prophet Muhammad, specifically linking Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq’s prophecy to Imam Musa al-Kadhim’s designation of Ali ibn Musa (Imam al-Rida). It underscores the Shia doctrine of *Nass* (explicit designation), where the Imam visually identifies his successor as a divine confirmation of the lineage's spiritual authority. The reference to 'seeing from oneself' emphasizes the intrinsic connection between the Imams as a single spiritual entity across generations.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 21 - It is narrated from Ahmad bin Idris from Ali bin Muhammad bin Qutaibah from Fadhl bin Shazan Nishapur from Muhammad bin Sinan and Safwan bin Yahya and Uthman bin Isa from Musa bin Bakar that he said:

I was in the company of Abu Ibrahim, Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s). The Imam said: Indeed, Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) said: A man is fortunate, who before his death sees his successor from his progeny. After that the Imam pointed out to his son, Ali and said: Almighty Allah has pointed out this son, who is from my life, as my successor.
